title: v0.2 Factual and deterministic foundation
description: One versioned recommendation algorithm: a manifest of every constant, protocol and prompt that shapes a recommendation, its id stamped on every row it writes, and a replay suite that proves the same games give byte-identical facts, profile and recommendations (ADR 0104).

title: v0.3 The evaluation lab
description: Every layer measured against its own ground truth: Lichess puzzle themes, Syzygy, lila's accuracy formula, synthetic players and anonymised real ones. Quality, cost and latency KPIs with 80% intervals, a history per algorithm version, and an Evaluation page on the site.

title: v0.4 Patterns and progression
description: One registry of versioned patterns (by motif, piece, phase, clock, opening, colour and after a loss), each admitted only after it passes its ground-truth suite, and a progression monitor that shows when a pattern started and whether it has recovered.

title: v0.5 Board, sound and clarity
description: The big UI round, from real-screenshot mockups the owner picks: sound in the trainer, a promotion picker and premoves, piece and board settings, an overview that leads with one trend and one focus, and "Why this?" on every recommendation.

title: v0.6 Practice habit and trainer depth
description: Turn the trainer into a daily habit and give every weekly focus a drill: a streak that forgives a rest day, an opt-in morning email, an ETA for "Is it working?", opening-trap lines, a clock budget and won positions played out against Maia.

title: v0.7 More players
description: Lichess accounts and PGN files as game sources, the app in more than one language, and the rating-band assumptions checked with players above 2000.

title: v1.0 MVP
description: The first complete release, declared in its own ADR: a stranger can sign up, link chess.com, practise daily, see whether it works, and delete everything when they leave.
